senses.gloss: m. (καμάρωτον, sub. ὄχημα, S.) vaulted, arch-covered carriage.—Pl. קַמְרוֹטִין, קַמְרוֹטָא (= καμάρωτα).
units: <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6:4:2">Cant. R. to VI, 4</cite> (expl. <cite ref="R00015"><he>צב</he></cite>, <cite ref="Numbers 7:3">Num. VII, 3</cite>, v. <cite ref="S01494"><he>קָמַר</he></cite>) <he>כמין ק׳ היו וכ׳</he> (not <he>קמרי׳</he>) the wagons were like the tilted carts, in order that the sacred vessels might not be split (through close packing), v. <cite ref="A02544"><he>אִסְקְפַסְטִי</he></cite>; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12:17">Num. R. s. 12</cite> <he>כמין כמרוסא היו כיפין עשויות</he> (read <cite ref="S01497"><he>קמרוטא</he></cite>, and strike out <he>כיפין</he> as a gloss expl. our w.); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:1:19">Y. Sabb. I, 2ᵈ</cite> <cite ref="S01501"><he>קמרסטא</he></cite>; Y. Succ. I, 52ᵃ top <cite ref="S01501"><he>קמרסטה</he></cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 713">Yalk. Num. 713</cite> <cite ref="S01501"><he>קמרסטא</he></cite> (obviously καμαραστα, fr. a verb καμαράζω).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 31">Gen. R. s. 31</cite> <he>כמין קומרוטין וכ׳</he> (some ed. <cite ref="S00409"><he>קומרוטון</he></cite>, Ar. <he>קמרוטין</he>) Noah’s ark was shaped like the tilted wagons, and it was so curved that the top was one cubit broad; Yalk. ib. 54 <he>קמרוטין</he>.
